issues.title: Join filters for RIGHT_SEMI/RIGHT_ANTI probe sides incl. DELIM_GET builds
issues.hypothesis: In q21 both decorrelated subqueries probe a full 60M-row lineitem scan against a small delim key set (708K distinct (orderkey,suppkey) of 15M orders). BuildProbeSideOptimizer (optimizer.cpp:247) runs before JOIN_FILTER_PUSHDOWN (optimizer.cpp:320), so the EXISTS-side inner join is already flipped SEMI->RIGHT_SEMI (probe=lineitem l2, build=DELIM_GET) and GenerateJoinFilters (join_filter_pushdown_optimizer.cpp:210-219) returns early for RIGHT_SEMI/RIGHT_ANTI -> no min/max or BF reaches the l2 scan; all 60M rows are hashed and probed (2.93M survive). Even where filters are generated, build_side_has_filter for a DELIM_GET rhs is computed on children[0] (the probe, unfiltered lineitem) -> false -> no BF; and CanUseBloomFilter (physical_hash_join.cpp:775) requires ht->conditions.size()==1 although these joins have 'l_orderkey = ... AND l_suppkey <> ...'. E0001 fixed the last two and the NOT EXISTS join dropped 0.92s->0.31s CPU, but the EXISTS (RIGHT_SEMI) side was untouched because of the early return. For RIGHT_SEMI and RIGHT_ANTI, probe rows without a build match never influence the output (only build rows are emitted, match flags are only set by matching probe rows), so filtering the probe side by the build key set is exactly as safe as for INNER/SEMI. The FIXME about inverting conditions applies to ANTI (probe-preserving), not RIGHT_ANTI.
issues.plan: 1) src/optimizer/join_filter_pushdown_optimizer.cpp GenerateJoinFilters: remove JoinType::RIGHT_SEMI and JoinType::RIGHT_ANTI from the early-return switch (keep LEFT/OUTER/ANTI/MARK/SINGLE), with a comment why it is safe. 2) Same file ~line 304: when rhs_child is LOGICAL_DELIM_GET set build_side_has_filter = true (a delim get is the deduplicated key set of the outer side, which is by construction a subset of the probe keys and is typically far smaller; the existing probe-est > HT-count check in CanUseBloomFilter still guards). 3) src/execution/operator/join/physical_hash_join.cpp JoinFilterPushdownInfo::CanUseBloomFilter: replace ht->conditions.size()==1 with ht->equality_predicate_columns.size()==1 (equalities come first; BF hashes only equality cols; non-equality conds still fail the cmp==COMPARE_EQUAL check). Verify PushBloomFilter uses conditions[0] / NullValuesAreEqual(0). Verify with EXPLAIN ANALYZE that both l2 and l3 lineitem scans show 'l_orderkey IN BF(...)' and their row counts drop to a few M; run full bench result checks. If the RIGHT_SEMI physical path in join_hashtable.cpp (lines ~994-1030, 1406-1436) makes any assumption about probe rows count, check it.
issues.expected_gain: q21 -8..-15% (E0001 alone gave -3.8..-7.5% from the NOT EXISTS side; the EXISTS side probes the same 60M rows against the same-size key set, so roughly doubles the saving).
issues.generality: Any EXISTS/IN/NOT EXISTS subquery that the planner flips to RIGHT_SEMI/RIGHT_ANTI (small outer key set, big inner table) — common in TPC-H q4/q20/q21/q22-style and decorrelated correlated subqueries with extra non-equality predicates. Could be slightly slower when the build key set covers most probe keys (BF hashing overhead ~7ns/row with no rejection); existing probe>build cardinality gate limits this.
issues.risk: Low-medium. Correctness: RIGHT_SEMI/RIGHT_ANTI semantics only depend on matching probe rows, so dropping non-matching probe rows is safe; NULL keys handled by existing filters_null_values logic. Perf risk: BF probe cost on probe sides with little rejection.

dispatch: Join filters for RIGHT_SEMI/RIGHT_ANTI probe sides incl. DELIM_GET builds
output.memory:
# Memory (planner, q21 specialisation run)

## Tooling facts
- dbe-tool profile / sql output is truncated (~150 lines / by width); deep subtrees of q21 not visible.
  Workaround: EXPLAIN ANALYZE sub-pieces of the query and grep "Total Time|[0-9]s |rows". Wide plans (delim joins) get cut by width too.
- `EXPLAIN (FORMAT json)` times out / prints nothing — don't retry. `$(...)` in commands is blocked.
- Operator timings in EXPLAIN ANALYZE are summed CPU across threads; Total Time is wall. First run of a scan is noisy (+50%); repeat.

## q21 plan shape (SF10, ~850-900ms hot)
- Main chain alone (no EXISTS/NOT EXISTS) = 0.64-0.74s wall → dominates.
- Current build ALREADY pushes `l_suppkey IN BF(s_suppkey)` + optional min/max into l1 lineitem scan: scan 3.38s CPU, 60M → 2.69M rows,
  FILTER receipt>commit → 1.70M, suppkey join → 1.52M (0.06s).
- orders scan (status='F' + BF(l_orderkey)) 0.41-0.64s CPU → 712K rows; orders⋈lineitem INNER join 0.69-0.93s CPU even with
  count(*) (no VARCHAR payload) — unexplained: 1.52M build/712K probe. Caching operator does compact small chunks
  (CachingPhysicalOperator, CACHE_THRESHOLD 64). Isolated test: 947K build/7.3M probe = 0.67s; 9K build/15M probe = 0.23s.
  Worth a dedicated investigation (where is build time: Sink partitioned append? Finalize insert misses?).
- Final HASH_GROUP_BY on s_name: 0.20s CPU for 735K rows/4009 groups.
- Subqueries: inner joins are lineitem ⋈ DELIM_GET on (l_orderkey =, l_suppkey <>); delim distinct 708K groups.
  EXISTS side is physical RIGHT_SEMI (probe = lineitem l2, build = delim), NOT EXISTS side ANTI-ish with lineitem probe.

## Scan cost facts (lineitem 60M rows, BitPacking, ~61K-row segments)
- 1-col int scan ~0.9s CPU (suppkey == partkey once warm); 2 date cols + col-col filter 0.93s+0.11s.
- Sparse Select after a selective filter saves little (bitpacking groups of 32 still decoded).
- BF hash+probe ~0.4s CPU per 60M rows.

## Codebase facts
- Optimizer order: BUILD_SIDE_PROBE_SIDE (optimizer.cpp:247) runs BEFORE JOIN_FILTER_PUSHDOWN (:320) → SEMI/ANTI already flipped
  to RIGHT_SEMI/RIGHT_ANTI when join filters are generated.
- GenerateJoinFilters (join_filter_pushdown_optimizer.cpp ~210) early-returns for LEFT/OUTER/ANTI/RIGHT_ANTI/RIGHT_SEMI/MARK/SINGLE.
  build_side_has_filter for DELIM_GET rhs uses IsFiltering(children[0]) (the probe side!) (~304).
- BF gate: JoinFilterPushdownInfo::CanUseBloomFilter physical_hash_join.cpp:761: rejects perfect HT, conditions.size()==1,
  EQUAL, build_side_has_filter, probe est > HT count. Deferred push in HashJoinFinalizeEvent::FinishEvent.
- BloomFilter impl: src/planner/filter/bloom_filter.cpp (1 sector of 64 bits, 4 bits/key, 12 bits/key sizing).
- OPTIONAL filters are only zonemap-checked then set always-true (row_group.cpp CheckZonemap) — no per-row cost.
- RowGroup::Scan (row_group.cpp ~694): filter columns first (adaptive order), then Select() other columns with sel.
- Perfect HJ: perfect_hash_join_executor.cpp CanDoPerfectHashJoin, MAX_BUILD_SIZE range 1,048,576.

## History
- E0001 RETIRED: BF for 1-equality + non-eq conds and DELIM_GET build → local -3.8..-7.5%, official +1% (noise). Only NOT EXISTS
  side benefited (0.92→0.31s) because EXISTS side is RIGHT_SEMI and skipped by GenerateJoinFilters. Good idea, incomplete.
- E0002 RETIRED: BF for sparse perfect HJ — filter worked but scan CPU rose (hash cost > savings). Bad idea for this data.
- Round 3: dispatched "Join filters for RIGHT_SEMI/RIGHT_ANTI probe sides incl. DELIM_GET builds" (= E0001 + RIGHT_SEMI/ANTI enable).

## Ideas for later
- Investigate orders⋈lineitem join 0.7-0.9s CPU (see above) — likely the next biggest fixable cost.
- Share l2/l3 lineitem scans or rewrite EXISTS(k= AND s<>) as per-key aggregate (big, risky).
- s_name group-by 0.2s: group on s_suppkey/compressed key instead of VARCHAR? (planner-level, risky).
